title: Super-admin password recovery silently does nothing: a tenant-less user's PasswordResetRequested event carries tenantId 'system', notification-service's UUID guard drops it (and acks), and the internal action-URL resolver would also reject the tenant-less token — the user sees success and no e-mail
rule_violated: category=contract-drift. Two subsystems disagree on how 'no tenant' is represented: auth-service encodes it as the sentinel string 'system' in a UUID-typed field, notification-service enforces 'tenantId is always a UUID' as a cross-tenant-leak guard. No shared type makes the platform-scope case representable, so the sentinel fails a validator written for a world where it does not exist — the same modelling gap FARM-HIGH-083 records on the outbox publish side.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05. A second, independent blocker sits behind the first: even past the UUID guard, requireNotificationService rejects an identity without tenantId and the action-token lookup filters WHERE tenantId = $2 while the super-admin token was saved with tenantId NULL. Fix direction (tier 1): make tenancy scope explicit in the event contract (discriminated scope: {kind:'tenant', tenantId} | {kind:'platform'}) so consumers must handle the platform case at compile time and the UUID guard applies only where a tenant is structurally required; the internal-API identity needs the matching platform-scope audience so tenant-less action tokens resolve. [RENUMBERED SEC-HIGH-057 -> SEC-HIGH-159 on 2026-09-05] Registered on the Faz 3 branch (PR #1424, claude/mobile-graphql-contract-0jj9jg) as SEC-HIGH-057; main had meanwhile allocated that sequence in the domain to SEC-HIGH-057 (Rust edge SignatureMode), so the row is re-registered as SEC-HIGH-159 when the branch took main. The original id names a live ledger row (sequence = identity) and cannot be an alias; the review file carries a Ledger ids table.

title: notification-service's auth event handler converts every failure into a normal return — a caught SMTP error, and null-returning PII/tenant/action-URL resolvers on any auth-service non-2xx — so the NATS consumer acks the message and the bus's own nak/backoff retry never engages; a transient outage loses invitation and password-reset e-mails for good
rule_violated: category=delivery-semantics. The bus documents the invariant explicitly ('Handler failures must NOT be swallowed while the message is acked… Route failures to retry/DLQ') and naks with exponential backoff on a thrown error; the handler never throws — it logs and returns on an exception, and its resolvers collapse permanent (404) and transient (5xx/network) failures alike into null. 'Logged and returned' is spellable as success, so the failure is invisible: no DLQ entry, no metric, no user-visible error.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05; the auth-service-outage path is deeper than the external review's cited catch block — the null-returning resolvers would survive deleting that catch. Fix direction (tier 1): make delivery outcome a value the transport reads rather than an exception a handler may absorb — IEventHandler.handle returns Ack | Retry(reason) | DeadLetter(reason), so a handler that wants to log must still choose an outcome; resolvers distinguish permanent from transient failure instead of returning null. Compounds with the super-admin reset defect: that drop is then acked as success.

title: The default MQTT ingestion path stores the calibrated, farm/pond-scoped reading but publishes the RAW, unscoped wire payload as the SensorReading event: the alert engine's fail-closed scope filter silently excludes every farm/pond-scoped rule and evaluates a value that is not the stored one, and an unmapped channel key upcasts to an empty reading that auto-resolves live incidents
rule_violated: category=event-contract. saveReading and publishSensorReadingEvent are two independent projections of one physical event built from two different inputs (calibrated SensorMetricInput rows with scope vs the untouched wire payload); every field that would catch the drift (farmId, pondId, tankId, flat readingXxx) is optional on SensorReadingEvent and no publish-side schema gate exists, so the producer omission type-checks and the alert engine's scope filter turns it into silent rule exclusion. The Rust-sidecar bridge and the GraphQL ingestion path already carry calibrated values and scope; only the two legacy MQTT/HTTP producers — still registered unconditionally, the SENSOR_SERVICE_PROFILE gate not yet wired — are wrong.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05; Phase 5 (VFD apply, SENSOR-CRITICAL-007) does not touch publishSensorReadingEvent. Life-safety relevant: a farm/pond-scoped dissolved-oxygen rule on the default ingestion path does not fire, and an unmapped key ('dissolved_oxygen', 'flow_rate', 'orp') closes an open INFO/LOW incident as 'returned to normal'. Fix direction (tier 1): no producer may mint a SensorReadingEvent from anything but persisted metric rows — saveReading returns the SensorMetricInput[] it wrote and one shared buildTypedReadingEvent(metrics, sensor) (the mapper the sidecar bridge already owns) is used by all four producers, publishing v3 flat fields; the v1 nested emission is deleted. Complementary: the alert engine distinguishes 'unscoped reading' from 'reading scoped to no farm' and rejects the former. Adjacent: SENSOR-MEDIUM-066/067. [RENUMBERED SENSOR-CRITICAL-106 -> SENSOR-CRITICAL-111 on 2026-09-05] Registered on the Faz 3 branch (PR #1424, claude/mobile-graphql-contract-0jj9jg) as SENSOR-CRITICAL-106; main had meanwhile allocated that sequence in the domain to SENSOR-HIGH-106, so the row is re-registered as SENSOR-CRITICAL-111 when the branch took main. The original id names a live ledger row (sequence = identity) and cannot be an alias; the review file carries a Ledger ids table.

title: A full deploy destroys the separately-installed monitoring stack and replaces it with a silent one: droplet-up.sh force-removes every container whose name contains 'aqua-' with no Compose-project scoping, then docker-compose.droplet.yml recreates the four monitoring containers under aqua-saas with the placeholder alertmanager.yml (smtp.invalid, receiver 'null') that checkout -f keeps unrendered
rule_violated: category=ownership. Two compose files claim the same four global container names, and the deploy's clean-slate step selects containers by a name substring instead of by the Compose project label that is the actual ownership boundary (the correct idiom is already used at droplet-up.sh:224); the monitoring compose's own header defends only against --remove-orphans. The Alertmanager config is rendered by mutating a git-tracked file while the consumer is a force-checked-out worktree at a different path, so the render is discarded by construction.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05. Net effect of one full deploy on a droplet running aqua-monitoring: the stack is reaped, recreated under aqua-saas pointing at smtp.invalid with a null default route, the Tier-1 memory gate in monitoring-up.sh is bypassed, TSDB history is orphaned in the other volume, and the runbooks' 'docker compose -p aqua-monitoring ps' reports a false outage. Nothing pages, nothing errors. Fix direction (tier 1): one owner per container — delete the four monitoring services from docker-compose.droplet.yml (docker-compose.monitoring.yml is the documented sole activation path); every container-selection step in droplet-up.sh filters by label=com.docker.compose.project=aqua-saas; render alertmanager.yml to a persistent gitignored path symlinked into the checkout like .env/certs (deploy-paths.sh:137-139) and mount that. OBS-HIGH-002's closure notes list the separate project as delivered and never noticed the duplicate; orphan-findings.md:8529 declares the render 'one script run away', which checkout -f makes false.

title: Uploaded object bytes are outside the recovery cut: MinIO lives in a bare local minio_data volume with no backup or replication path (the repo's only mc command is a purge), and the PostgreSQL PITR/restore proof and its production stop-line never mention object storage, so a restore that reports success leaves dangling keys to photos, certificates and attachments
rule_violated: category=dr-scope. The DR programme was scoped to 'the database' rather than 'the durable state'; because object references are stored in PostgreSQL, a green PITR proof looks complete while the referenced bytes are gone with the host. The plan's own current-state table records the gap (BR-3, exit target 2026-08-28, now passed) but it is the one architectural conclusion there with no finding id, so it is invisible to the sweep, the deadline machinery and any merge gate.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-05 (external review claim 7). Full BR-3 (versioned Spaces replica + AWS Object Lock WORM vault + version-bound references + the three-state adapter protocol) is the end state and is gated on BR-1 secrets. Smallest architecturally sound step now: an object-storage-replica capability in dr-activation.json (state not-activated, unlockPhase BR-3) with a bucket-versioning/replication probe lane, so every backup/PITR run warns 'PRODUCTION HAS NO object-storage-replica', and the restore-drill stop-line names object-version parity as a required condition — a PostgreSQL-only restore can no longer be read as a platform restore. Claim 6 of the same review (backup activation/restore proof) is already covered by INFRA-HIGH-033/034/035/073 and is an operator-evidence gap, not a code gap; note dr-activation.json cites ORPHAN-HIGH-563 which is prose-only, not a registry id.
